title: Primary 2 Addition and Subtraction within 1000
seo_title: P2 Addition and Subtraction Worksheets: Free Primary 2 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Addition and subtraction algorithms (up to 3 digits); mental calculation of a 3-digit number and ones/tens/hundreds
meta_desc: Free P2 maths practice: mental sums, 3-digit addition and subtraction with renaming, checking answers and bar model word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Line up the ones, then rename when a place has 10 or more.
key_sub: 367 + 258: 7 + 8 = 15, write 5 and rename 1 ten; 6 + 5 + 1 = 12, write 2 and rename 1 hundred; 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 625.
body_html:
The idea: ones with ones, tens with tens

A 3-digit number has hundreds, tens and ones. Add or subtract the same places. When a place has 10 or more, rename 10 of them as 1 of the next place.

Mental calculation

To add or take away tens, only the tens digit changes. To add or take away hundreds, only the hundreds digit changes.

Number sentenceWhat changesAnswer
345 + 30tens: 4 + 3 = 7375
562 − 200hundreds: 5 − 2 = 3362
386 + 40tens: 8 + 4 = 12, rename 10 tens as 1 hundred426

Add with renaming

Write ones under ones. Start with the ones on the right. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and rename 10 as 1 of the next place. Write the small 1 at the top of the next column.

Subtract with renaming

Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. If the top digit is smaller, rename 1 of the next place as 10.

Across 0: if there are 0 tens, rename 1 hundred as 10 tens first. Then rename 1 ten as 10 ones. The 0 tens become 9 tens.

Check with the inverse

Is 500 − 168 = 332 correct?

Add back what you took away: 332 + 168 = 500. You get the first number, so it is correct.

Answer: Yes

Word problems: draw a bar model

A part-whole model shows two parts and a whole. Find the whole: add. Find a part: subtract. A comparison model shows two bars. Find how many more or fewer: subtract.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
No renaming: 367 + 258 = 515Write the renamed 1 in the next column and add it: 625
Smaller digit from the larger: 452 − 178 = 326Take the bottom digit from the top digit. Rename when the top is smaller: 274
Making 0 tens into 10 tens: 500 − 168 = 3421 ten moves to the ones, so 10 tens become 9 tens: 332
Columns not lined up: 346 + 52 = 866Put ones under ones: 346 + 52 = 398

faq.q: What do P2 pupils learn about addition and subtraction?
faq.a: In Primary 2, pupils add and subtract numbers up to 1000. They use mental calculation, the column method with renaming, and bar models for word problems.

faq.q: What does renaming mean in Singapore maths?
faq.a: Renaming means changing 10 of one place into 1 of the next place, such as 10 ones into 1 ten. Some older books call it carrying or borrowing.

faq.q: How do I help my child subtract across 0, like 500 − 168?
faq.a: Rename 1 hundred as 10 tens, then 1 ten as 10 ones. 500 becomes 4 hundreds 9 tens 10 ones, so 500 − 168 = 332.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. The MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus has Primary 2 pupils add and subtract up to 3 digits and do mental calculation with ones, tens and hundreds. These skills are used in every level up to the PSLE in Primary 6.

items.e: 30 is 3 tens. Only the tens change: 4 + 3 = 7. 345 + 30 = 375.

items.q: What is 100 more than 875?
items.e: 100 more means 1 more hundred. 8 hundreds become 9 hundreds. The tens and ones stay the same: 975.

items.q: What is 10 less than 603?
items.e: 603 has 0 tens. Rename 1 hundred as 10 tens. Take away 1 ten: 9 tens are left, and 5 hundreds. 603 − 10 = 593. (693 forgets that 6 hundreds become 5 hundreds.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 456 + ? = 486
items.e: The hundreds and ones stay the same. The tens go from 5 to 8. That is 3 tens: 30. Check: 456 + 30 = 486.

items.q: Find the missing number: 924 − ? = 524
items.e: The tens and ones stay the same. The hundreds go from 9 to 5. That is 4 hundreds: 400. Check: 924 − 400 = 524.

items.q: Count on by hundreds. What is 218 + 300?
items.e: 300 is 3 hundreds. Only the hundreds change: 2 + 3 = 5. 218 + 300 = 518.

items.q: Which one is equal to 640?
items.e: 590 + 50: 9 tens + 5 tens = 14 tens. Rename 10 tens as 1 hundred. 5 hundreds become 6 hundreds, with 4 tens left. 590 + 50 = 640. The others are 595, 650 and 1090.

items.e: Line up the ones and start on the right. Ones: 1 + 8 = 9. Tens: 4 + 0 = 4. Hundreds: 6 + 2 = 8. Answer: 849.

items.q: The library lent out 296 books in May. In June, it lent out 148 more books than in May. How many books did it lend out in June?
items.e: More than in May, so add. 296 + 148 = 444. Check: 444 − 148 = 296.

items.q: Mr Rahman needs 750 lights for a Deepavali display at the community centre. He has put up 487 lights. How many more lights must he put up?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. To find the other part, subtract. 750 − 487 = 263. Check: 263 + 487 = 750.

items.q: Xin Yi has 342 cards. Ethan has 186 cards. Which number sentence finds how many more cards Xin Yi has?
items.e: How many more means find the difference. Take the smaller number from the bigger number. The number sentence is 342 − 186 = ? and the answer is 156.

items.q: Chloe walked 465 m from her HDB block to the MRT station. Then she walked 278 m to the library. How far did she walk altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. 465 + 278 = 743. Check: 743 − 278 = 465.

items.q: A durian seller sold 238 durians. He had 167 durians left. How many durians did he have at first?
items.e: The durians sold and the durians left make the whole. Add: 238 + 167 = 405. Check: 405 − 238 = 167.
